title: Why You Feel So Heavy After Deep Sleep
hook: Waking up from deep sleep can make your body feel incredibly heavy.

narration.text: Waking up from deep sleep can make your body feel incredibly heavy.
This groggy sensation is called sleep inertia.
It happens when your brain hasn't fully transitioned to wakefulness.
Parts of your brain are still in a sleep-like state, especially the prefrontal cortex.
This temporary confusion makes it hard to think clearly or move quickly.
It's why you might struggle to get out of bed immediately.
Sleep inertia is strongest after you've been in slow-wave sleep.
So, how long does it usually take for you to shake off that grogginess?

description: Ever wondered why your body feels like lead after waking from a deep sleep? This short explains sleep inertia, the fascinating reason behind that groggy, heavy feeling. Learn how your brain's transition from sleep impacts your morning.
topic: Why your body feels heavy and you struggle to move after waking from deep sleep, explaining sleep inertia.
